name: Stacks and status on the Reviews index

pr.title: Group stacked pull requests on the Reviews index and show each one's status
pr.head: 8193671d77a0c3c62c851392f922fdbb325ec4cc

summary: Projector's site has a Reviews index: one row per pull request that has a published summary, linking to that summary's page. Before this change the index listed rows newest first and marked a stacked pull request with a "Stacked on #N" line, so the layers of one stack were scattered wherever their numbers fell. The index also did not say whether a pull request was still open or what its latest review found.

1. It groups each stack. The build orders the rows in site.json so that each stack's pull requests sit together, from the layer on the default branch up, at the position where the stack's newest pull request would sort. The page draws a stack's rows in one table body with no divider between them.
  2. It shows each pull request's status. A row reads Merged or Closed once the pull request is, and otherwise shows the verdict of the newest Projector review of its newest head: Clean, Changes requested, or Unreviewed. The summary page's header now shows Merged and Closed the same way.
  3. It hides finished pull requests by default. Merged and closed rows stay hidden until the reader checks Show merged and closed. A stack's open layers still show together when a layer beneath them has merged.

To keep the summary page and the site drawing these the same way, the status, the time format, the credit line, and the HTML escaper move to the top of summary.ts as global functions. Every site page now loads summary.js before site.js, and on a page with no summary summary.js returns after one lookup.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Stack: pull requests where each one's base branch is the head branch of the one beneath it. Siblings on the same base belong to one stack.
  • site.json: the data file the build writes and site.js reads to draw every view of the site.
  • stack field: on each review row, the number of the first review in its stack, shared by every row in it, or null when the row stands alone.
  • Newest head: the most recently published version of a pull request's summary.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The Projector review of 8193671d7 is clean, with no finding threads. It suggests one wording fix in docs/cli.md, noted on that file below.

groups.title: The order and fields of site.json
groups.kicker: The build sorts reviews into stacks and records each one's status
intro: The Python build decides the order of the index. A new stack_groups walks the reviewed pull requests from newest to oldest. For each one not yet placed, it takes the whole stack from stack_rows, the same function that lists a stack in a summary's sidebar, and keeps the members that have a review here. So the index and the sidebar always agree on a stack's members and order.

Each row in site.json now carries stack, the pull request's state, and its newest head's review, and drops the old head and stackedOn fields. updated becomes a full UTC timestamp instead of a date, so the page can show it in the reader's time zone.

checks.text: Nothing outside site.ts reads site.json, and tsc accepts the new SiteReview type, so no reader still expects head or stackedOn. Checked by searching src/ and running npm run check.

files.note: stack_groups orders the entries; review_row writes each row of site.json.

checks.text: Every reviewed pull request lands in exactly one group: walking down bases from any member of a stack reaches the same bottom, so stack_rows returns the same members from each of them. A base pull request with no review here is left out of the group. Traced by hand, including a cycle in bases.
The entries now come in stack order, so a project's own list of reviews is sorted again here to stay newest first.

files.note: Adds the shared PullState and ReviewStatus types and reshapes SiteReview to match the new rows.

groups.title: Helpers both pages share
groups.kicker: summary.js now holds the status, time, credit, and escaping helpers
intro: The summary page and the site's own pages are drawn by two scripts. This change moves four helpers out of the summary renderer's private scope to the top of summary.ts, where they become global functions: esc, creditHtml, localTime, and statusHtml. site.ts drops its own copy of esc and calls these instead.
statusHtml puts Merged or Closed ahead of any verdict, and returns nothing when the build could not ask GitHub, so an unknown status never reads as Unreviewed.

files.note: The shared helpers at the top, and an early return when the page has no #summary.

checks.text: On a site page with no #summary, summary.js makes one getElementById call and returns before it renders, fetches, or adds a listener. SharedHelperTests checks this with a proxied document, and it passed at this head.
The link this builds matches what the header's old ext(...) call built: same class, target="_blank", and rel="noopener".

files.note: Adds the Merged and Closed colors for the light and dark themes.

groups.title: The Reviews index
groups.kicker: Stacks share a table body; finished pull requests wait behind a checkbox
intro: showReviews now draws a Show merged and closed checkbox when any row is merged or closed, and redraws the table when the reader checks it. reviewsTable groups consecutive rows that share a non-null stack into one tbody class="stack", which the CSS draws with no divider between rows.

The table gains a Status column and loses the Head column and the "Stacked on" line. The Updated column shows the newest head's publish time in a <time> element. The footer on every site page now reads "Generated by Projector", like the summary page's credit.

files.note: The new table, the checkbox, and the shared footer.

checks.text: Hiding a merged middle layer leaves the open layers above it in one table body, because the grouping keys on stack, which every row of a stack shares. ReviewsViewTests covers it, and passed at this head.
A row with no state means the build could not ask GitHub. isDone is false for it, so it is always shown.

files.note: Baseline-aligns the row cells and removes the divider inside a stack's table body.

groups.title: Compiled JavaScript
groups.kicker: The committed output of npm run build
intro: The site serves compiled JavaScript from site/assets/, so the change commits it. Running npm ci, npm run check, and npm run build at this head left both files unchanged.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: New view tests under node, and the CLI reference
intro: The tests run the compiled functions under node with stubs for the DOM. They cover the build's stack order, the rows' state and verdict, the table bodies with and without the checkbox, the time format under TZ=UTC, and the guarantee that summary.js does nothing on a page without a summary. The full suite ran 527 tests at this head, all passing.
docs/cli.md describes the new index and the header's Merged and Closed status.

checks.text: The review suggests dropping "open" here. stack_bases never checks a pull request's state, so a layer whose base pull request has merged stays in that stack, on the index and in the sidebar. The text before this change said the same.
